simple.meaning: רָפַק (râphaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to recline.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Song of Solomon, beginning at Song of Songs 8:5. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.

definitions.full: H7514. raphaq [ רָפַק ] verb Hithpa`el support oneself, lean (Ethiopic reclinare, accumbere ad mensam; compare Arabic be Gentle, bind camel's arm to prevent going quickly ; , Late Hebrew מַרְמַּק , Jewish-Aramaic מַרְמְּקָא , elbow ); — Participle feminine מִתְרַמֶּקֶת Song 8:5 (with עַל person). רפשׂ see רפס . above רפשׁ (√ of following; Late Hebrew רֶפֶשׂ = Biblical Hebrew; Schulth 71f. compare Arabic talk or act obscenely , and a Syriac slag, refuse (not in PS Brock and others)).
